messages:
maya: Alert: eu-west1 inference fleet reporting sudden pod evictions + network packet drops across 3 racks. Backpressure spiking, ~35% capacity lost. I recommend emergency per-customer soft caps + shift non-critical traffic to eu-west2. Thoughts?

oncall-bot: INCIDENT-1845127890 created: eu-west1 degraded network -> serving capacity loss. Paging oncall. :ambulance:

siva: Oncall here. Confirming SLO impact: p95 latencies up ~400ms for streaming sessions. Can we set per-customer soft caps to 30 concurrent requests and 100k tokens/min for embeddings as a starting point?

liam: Prefer tokens/min over concurrent for bursty customers. Suggest 100k tokens/min + 30 concurrent for general noisy tenants. For top-tier customers, enable targeted region_failover so they don't see failures.

maya: Agree. Plan: run admin script to apply softcaps for noisy customers (>10k req/day), shift ~20% routing weight to eu-west2 for non-critical traffic, and open a canary for low-priority batch queues. I'll coordinate with ops-jen to run the commands.

ops-jen: Command I'm about to run to apply softcaps:

```bash
# apply softcaps via admin API
curl -s -X POST https://admin.redwood/api/v1/quotas/apply \\n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN\" \\n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\n  -d '{"scope":"customers:hot","concurrent":30,"tokens_per_min":100000,"reason":"eu-west1 capacity emergency"}'
```

siva: I'll take routing changes. Plan: add eu-west2 weight +25% for non-SPOT, non-critical routes, and set retry/backoff for streaming clients to prefer fallback earlier.

liam: Also recommend fallback to the smaller quantized model (x16) for low-tier customers to reduce memory pressure and token generation time. That will reduce GPU working set and help evictions.

ops-jen: Softcaps applied to 34 customers (response: 200). Immediate effect: inbound QPS for those tenants dropped ~20%, p95 latency improving by ~180ms. Still seeing packet drops on rack-12 (eth1 flaps).

maya: Okay start graceful evacuation of spot instances on rack-12 and migrate stateful caches where possible. ops-jen please start drain sequence and mark rack-12 for hardware ops.

ops-jen: Drain started for rack-12 pools. Commands used: 
```bash
# drain nodes in rack-12
redwoodctl nodes drain --selector rack=rack-12 --timeout 300
```
ETA ~10m to finish. Will leave per-customer caps in place until we see stable p95.

alexa: Support: posting status update to status.redwood.ai and emailing top-10 noisy customers with the standard emergency template. Draft link: https://docs.redwood/status-templates/eu-west1-evac

oncall-bot: Alert: routing fallback succeeded for ~68% of retried requests (metric: fallback_success_rate). Monitoring continues.

siva: Suggest we convert these emergency softcaps into temporary quotas (windowed) and schedule an automated rollback in 60 minutes unless manually extended. Any objections?

liam: No objections. +1

maya: Locking rollback job for +3600s as a safeguard (keeps caps on until then). If packet drops persist we escalate to full region failover. I'll update the incident doc and post follow-up in 15m.

oncall-bot: Incident severity set to SEV2. Next update planned in 15 minutes.
